heroHeadline: Netanyahu-Trump Alliance Fractures Over Gaza and Iran — Sources Say Both Sides 'Screwed Each Other Pretty Badly'
heroSubtitle: Israeli airstrikes on Gaza City on May 8, 2026 killed at least 33 Palestinians in one of the deadliest single-day tolls since the October 2025 ceasefire, hitting the last operating restaurant in Gaza City and a crowded adjacent market. An IDF strike also killed a son of Hamas chief negotiator Khalil Al-Hayya — the fifth member of his immediate family harmed by Israeli fire since the ceasefire. The cumulative Palestinian death toll since the October 10, 2025 ceasefire now surpasses 870. Israel's security cabinet convened on May 8 to formally deliberate resuming full-scale military operations in Gaza after Hamas rejected the Board of Peace's five-stage disarmament roadmap; ministers representing the far-right bloc argued for immediate war resumption. Video footage circulated showing an Israeli settler using his vehicle to block a Palestinian ambulance transporting a critically ill patient south of Nablus. Bloomberg reported Israel is 'tightening its grip on Gaza as the deadlock with Hamas persists' — with the IDF now controlling approximately 60% of Gaza territory. The Board of Peace's Nickolay Mladenov told the UN Security Council the diplomatic window was 'rapidly closing.'
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OCHA, IDF, Gaza Ministry of Health, B'Tselem, ICC, ICJ, Reuters, Al Jazeera, OHCHR, UNRWA, Times of Israel, Haaretz, Bloomberg, Jerusalem Post, Human Rights Watch, Save the Children, Amnesty International, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are subject to ongoing verification. The conflict has persisted since Israeli independence on May 14, 1948.
